instruction.text: Select the entrance to this Anglo-Saxon house.
Look at the inside of this house and select true or false.

atoms.a: Animals stayed inside the house with the family.
Anglo-Saxons slept outside the house to stay cool.
Anglo-Saxons kept a fire on inside the house.

feedback.end: With so many things in one room, this would probably have been very smelly, but it helped to keep everyone warm and safe. Having a fire indoors could make the house quite smoky though!

instruction.text: Drag the ingredients into the pot to make pottage.

atoms.b: You just made a stew called ((++pottage porridge)), consisting of vegetables, grains, water, herbs and sometimes a bit of ((++meat jam)).
This is what most Anglo-Saxons ate on a ((++daily yearly)) basis, along with some eggs and milk from the animals.

instruction.text: Can you find the man playing the harp at this feast?
Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Chiefs spent lots of money on feasts and there was a lot of roasted meat. Guests were still expected to bring their own bowls though!
At feasts, chiefs would entertain their guests with stories, and someone might play an instrument like a lyre or a harp.

atoms.a: What do you think chiefs ate at their feasts?
b: ++lots of roasted meat with ale, wine, stew and bread

instruction.text: Select the hut to learn more.

feedback.end: After all that eating, Anglo-Saxons needed somewhere to go to the toilet! Huts similar to this were put on top of holes in the ground. They had to move the huts quite often because it got so smelly!
